hypothesis: Global full-frame resizing devotes few pixels to the dorsal surface, while global depth range includes pen background. A central native-image crop and a row-relative depth channel may preserve relevant local relief without requiring RGB-depth pixel registration.
sampling: Same deterministic maximum 12 decoded-RGB representatives per episode as all earlier evaluation; no frame rejected by quality or model output
crop: Central 50 percent of native width and central 90 percent of native height, defined before model outcomes; RGB and depth crops computed independently
depth_global: 1st/99th percentile of valid positive pixels, clipped to [0,1], invalid=0
relative_relief: Subtract each row's valid median, divide by frame-wide 90th minus 10th valid percentile of residuals, clip signed residual to [-1,1], encode as [0,1] with invalid=0. Third channel is the validity mask. No physical depth units or calibrated anatomy are claimed.
features: Fully frozen ImageNet ResNet18, 512-dimensional mean pool, L2 normalized episode mean
controls: depth central crop with repeated global-normalised channel
depth central crop with global depth, relative relief, validity channels
regressor: RBF SVR; same fixed 3x4 inner-validation bandwidth and C grid as full-image frozen references; alpha in [0.01,0.1,1,10], C=1/alpha; bandwidth multiplier in [0.5,1,2]; epsilon=0.1; training pairwise median squared distance sets bandwidth
secondary_probe: Ridge on acquisition metadata only, train-only standardisation; no biological interpretation of metadata prediction
scope: New preprocessing candidate tested against frozen, capacity-matched controls; no segmentation ground truth, no claim of universal anatomical localisation, no confirmatory external depth cohort
